newsitem.title: USA: Minsur smelter seen slashing tin costs.
newsitem.headline: Minsur smelter seen slashing tin costs.

text.p: Minsur's new Funsur tin smelter which began production last month is set to produce metal at less than half the industry's average cost, an analyst said.

"It was a big concern in the market that the Ausmelt technology was not going to work, but I think it's been proved otherwise," mining analyst Josilu Carbonel of Lima brokerage Santander Investment told Reuters.
Minsur's $30 million smelter has a production capacity of 15,000 tonnes of metal a year. The company aims to raise this to 20,000 tonnes by installing oxygen enrichment equipment.
Minsur is refining at the rate of 200 tonnes per month at present as the plant tackles teething problems and edges towards full production next year.
The company is Peru's only tin producer and the fourth largest in the world, accounting for 11 percent of global production.
On Tuesday Santander initiated coverage of Minsur shares and issued a buy recommendation.
The world's tin industry is taking a close interest in Minsur's new greenfield smelter which uses technology devised by Ausmelt AMiET.AX of Australia.
The technology failed when grated onto an existing tin smelter in the Netherlands.
Successfully operational, the smelter lowers the industry cost curve at a stroke, giving high cost producers much food for thought.
Carbonel said Minsur tolled refined some 12,000 tonnes of tin concentrates at Vinto's smelter in Bolivia this year. The cost of smelting and refining is about $600 per tonne.
Minsur expected its new smelter to smelt and refine concentrates for $300 per tonne or below, Carbonel said, adding that the industry's average refining cost was $700 to $800 per tonne.
Santander said Minsur's total production costs and depreciation were already the lowest in the world at an estimated $1,853 per tonne this year and were forecast to dip to $1,178 in 1998.
The present average production cost at other tin smelters was $2,500 to $3,000 per tonne, Carbonel said.
London Metal Exchange cash tin settled at $5,873 per tonne on Wednesday.
Carbonel said apart from savings from refining inhouse with its new, low cost smelter, further savings were also planned by using less energy on the mining side.
As Minsur's new smelter reaches full output next year, the company does not yet know if it will renew its tolling contract with Vinto for 1997.
"They are still studying the possibility of not renewing the contract," Carbonel said.
Prior to the new smelter coming on stream, all of Minsur's concentrates were either tolled at Vinto or sold to smelters in Malaysia.

Santander forecast that Minsur will produce 49,767 tonnes of concentrates (grading 50 percent tin) this year, and 60,987 tonnes in 1997 and 1998 when the company will account for 17 percent of world production.
In-house refined tin production will reach 700 tonnes this year during the smelter start-up phase, Santander said.
-- Huw Jones, New York Commodities 212-859-1646
